content:
incident-bot: Incident INF-2026-03-18-DNS-FAILOVER created. Priority: P1. Affected region: ap-northeast-1. Short: GPU pool degradation + DNS cache preventing traffic shift.

ajay: saw a 60% drop in available GPU nodes at 18:02 UTC. Autoscaler removed some pods but public traffic is still routing to ap-northeast IPs.

kate: confirm. our DNS records for service.redwood.ai still resolve to ap-northeast IPs for many resolvers. TTL was 300s set yesterday.

sara: any chance of a quick TTL drop? provider docs say minimal TTL for ALIAS is 60s but rate limits apply.

ben: ran a quick global check:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 service.redwood.ai A
203.0.113.12
```
multiple ASNs still returning 203.0.113.12 (ap-northeast). Dig trace shows cached NS at ISP level.

lucas: edge steering path: we can force CDN to originate from fallback region without touching DNS. That will handle most HTTP traffic immediately.

ajay: good. but TLS/ALPN SNI and client pinning may still hit old endpoints. We should also add SDK fallback to the client: alternate endpoint host that bypasses DNS.

kate: action plan:
- reduce DNS TTL to 60 (if provider accepts) via API
- enable CDN steering and set weight to 100% fallback region
- notify top partners to purge caches
- run global dns sweep script and collect stuck ASNs
I'll attempt TTL change now.

sara: I'll prepare the ASN sweep and a list for outreach.

ops-bot: Deploy started: CDN steering config update (deploy id cdn-4523). ETA 3m.

ajay: TTL update attempt:
```
curl -X PATCH "https://api.dns-provider.example/zones/redwood/records/service.redwood.ai"  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DNS_TOKEN"  -H "Content-Type: application/json"  -d '{"ttl":60}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Provider accepted TTL=60 but warns about propagation delay up to previous TTL for some resolvers.

ben: after TTL change, re-run dig. still many return old IP. Looks like ~12% of queries worldwide still pointing to ap-northeast.

lucas: CDN steering deploy succeeded. Monitoring shows 70% of HTTP traffic now served from fallback region despite DNS cache.

kate: reminder: lowering TTL helps for future incidents, but we can't rely on instant propagation. We'll add a pre-incident step in the playbook to keep TTL=60 for high-availability records permanently (with cost/rate-limit caveats).

sara: also propose adding a health-check-based DNS failover entry that uses our DNS provider's health checks to flip targets automatically.

ajay: postmortem note: add client SDK fallback and document edge-steering fallback. For this incident, raising to recovery: traffic stable, errors down to baseline.

kate: closing actions: create runbook PR with steps & scripts, update partner outreach template, schedule a drill next week.

incident-bot: Incident INF-2026-03-18-DNS-FAILOVER moved to resolved by kate. Duration: 43m.
